audience.programmeDescription: Leiden’s English-taught Urban Studies degree combines social science, humanities and environmental research to study how cities work and change. Students investigate urban sustainability, safety, health and diversity through thematic courses, field and research methods, and a graduation project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The three UCR options explore cities through governance and society, climate resilience and spatial planning, or community safety and health. They share some methods and subject matter with Leiden. Leiden provides a dedicated urban studies core, city-specific research training and a required graduation pathway.

curriculum.routeLabel: Sustainable City and Safe City, with the Urban Arts, Culture and Society thesis pathway
curriculum.limitation: This 180 EC example includes one thematic and one methods elective per semester in year two. Year three includes 30 EC of open study and a thesis pathway with a seminar and research lab.

componentNotes.urb-y3-thesis-seminar: Entry requires 100 EC including two thematic and two methods electives, plus Reading the City.
componentNotes.urb-y3-thesis: The thesis follows the seminar proposal and carries 10 EC.

notes.text: Leiden offers an integrated Urban Studies sequence with city-specific foundations, thematic lectures, electives, methods, a research lab and a compulsory thesis. UCR can construct three coherent urban-focused programmes from governance, sociology, law, health, sustainability, environmental science and research methods, but it does not reproduce the same dedicated Urban Studies core; shared rows indicate substantive overlap rather than course equivalence.

GOSGATE102.name: Law, Society & Justice
GOSGATE102.text: Law, Society & Justice examines legal, social and normative perspectives on law. Students compare legal traditions and study public and private law, human rights, justice, social control and change, race and gender. Case briefs, demand letters and mock trials develop legal reasoning, while a family-law topic supports the design of a socio-legal research proposal.

ENSDELT312.name: Governance of Sustainability
ENSDELT312.text: This course examines sustainability through the lens of governance: “a process of rule-making and collective decision-making that includes both governmental and non-governmental actors in shaping public policy” (Fenger & Bekkers, 2016). Taking this lens, we ask questions such as how are sustainability policies on the local, national, and international level made and enforced? Which actors represent which interests, and which are most influential? How is public opinion on sustainability shaped, and how does public opinion shape politics? What, at the end of the day, determines effective policy for sustainability? By the end of this course, you will have gained a deep appreciation of the complexity of the governance dimension of sustainability, and have developed the theoretical and practical understanding to critically assess mainstream policy decisions.

BENECON312.name: Econometrics
BENECON312.text: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. In this course you learn three estimators—Ordinary Least Squares, Generalized Least Squares, and Instrumental Variables—and three tests—t-test, F-test, and LM-test. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.
